PROJECT PLANNING

A Mobilisation Readiness Review for Ground Engineering Works

Confirm the practical prerequisites before the planned start becomes a costly wait.

In this insight

Define readiness against the proposalVerify evidence rather than promisesInclude people and communicationClose the review with a decisionFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Define readiness against the proposal

A mobilisation date is only useful if the site can support the planned work. Review the conditions assumed in the accepted proposal: access, available area, enabling work, information, approvals and interfaces. Turn those assumptions into a short readiness checklist. The aim is to identify specific outstanding items, not to create another meeting that repeats the programme without testing it.

Verify evidence rather than promises

For each prerequisite, identify the relevant document, inspection or confirmation and the person authorised to accept it. A statement that an item will be ready soon should remain an open action. Separate technical approvals from logistical readiness so one is not mistaken for the other. This gives the team an accurate picture of what can proceed and what remains dependent on further work.

Include people and communication

Confirm the delivery contacts, supervision arrangements, document routes and escalation process. Ensure the teams understand the current sequence and where to find authorised information. A technically prepared site can still suffer avoidable delay if personnel do not know who can resolve a query or approve the next stage. Clear communication is a practical part of readiness.

Close the review with a decision

Record which activities are ready, which are conditional and what remains blocked. Give each open action an owner and a required date. Where the start plan changes, document the commercial and programme implications through the agreed process. The review should create a shared, evidence-based view of mobilisation, reducing the chance that equipment and people arrive before the necessary conditions are in place.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Test the proposal’s readiness assumptions.
  • Use evidence to close prerequisites.
  • Record conditional and blocked activities clearly.
